line.text: Two baskets by the couch. She's been at this a while. Every fold lands at the same angle.
Basket's yours. Left side. I wasn't going to fold around it.
Machine was running. Half-empty drum is a waste.
She matches two of your socks and sets them on your pile without looking up.
Your towels were taking up the rack. Also your towels were damp. Both problems, one solution.
Don't make it a thing. It's laundry. It's the most solved problem in the apartment.
Her tail has gone completely still. She folds the same shirt twice.

choice.prompt: She's waiting for the verdict, whatever it is.

options.text: Fold the rest of the basket beside her. Say nothing.

reaction.text: She watches your hands for one fold, then goes back to hers.
Left side is shirts. Right is everything that doesn't matter.

options.text: Thanks. You didn't have to do mine.

reaction.text: Her ears flatten fast. She smooths them with a hand like she's fixing her fringe.
It wasn't for you. It was for the drum.

options.text: You look wrecked. Did you sleep at all last night?

reaction.text: The fold in her hands stops mid-shirt.

options.text: So what do I owe you for this?

reaction.text: Her tail tucks before her face moves at all.
Nothing. It's a washing machine, not a favor.

desc: Laundry night: she folds with machine precision, your things included, and does not mention it.
